title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Representatives
tiers.description: The Board, Management Board and employees of Judo (temporary and permanent), and any other person or class of persons the Board determines. All Representatives are bound by the insider trading prohibition, the Blackout Period dealing ban, and the outright prohibitions on short-term/speculative trading, hedging and margin lending/secured financing.

tiers.name: Restricted Class
tiers.description: Board members, Management Board members, and any other person or class of persons the Board determines. Unlike other Representatives, this class must obtain prior written clearance to deal outside a Blackout Period.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Board; a subset of the Restricted Class. Additionally must provide the Company Secretary with written notification of any trade within 2 business days for ASX/ASIC disclosure purposes.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions entered into to limit the economic risk associated with holding Judo Securities

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine any other Blackout Period from time to time; the policy does not state whether such additional blackouts are confidential, but a refusal of clearance during any blackout must be kept confidential by the person who sought it.

rules.detail: Derivatives are expressly included in the definition of Securities with no venue limitation, so an OTC put/call over Judo shares is dealing in Securities. Restricted Class members must obtain prior written clearance (from the CEO, Board Chair, Audit Committee Chair or Company Secretary as applicable) before dealing outside a Blackout Period, and cannot deal at all during Blackout Periods except in exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: Securities includes shares; options; rights; debentures (including convertible notes); derivatives; options over an unissued share in, or debenture of, a company; ... and other Division 3 financial products as defined in section 1042A of the Corporations Act.

rules.detail: Representatives who are not members of the Restricted Class do not require clearance to deal (including in derivatives, which are Securities) outside a Blackout Period, though the insider trading prohibition and the outright bans on hedging and margin lending/secured financing still apply.
rules.evidence: Representatives who are not members of the Restricted Class do not require clearance to deal in Judo Securities outside a Blackout Period.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on hedging transactions that limit the economic risk of holding Judo Securities. Applies to all Representatives regardless of tier, with no distinction between vested and unvested holdings and no clearance carve-out.
rules.evidence: Entering into hedging transactions to limit the relevant person's exposure. Hedging transactions means transactions entered into to limit the economic risk associated with holding Judo Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement would be dealing in a Security (Division 3 financial product) requiring clearance for Restricted Class members outside a Blackout Period; if the structure involves granting security over the shares to obtain financing, it instead falls within the outright ban in section 9(c).
rules.evidence: Securities includes ... other Division 3 financial products as defined in section 1042A of the Corporations Act.

rules.detail: For non-Restricted-Class Representatives, an unsecured monetisation structure would not require clearance outside a Blackout Period, but any structure using the shares as security for financing is independently banned by section 9(c) regardless of tier.
rules.evidence: Representatives who are not members of the Restricted Class do not require clearance to deal in Judo Securities outside a Blackout Period.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named. It is dealing in Securities within the meaning of the Corporations Act and would require clearance outside a Blackout Period for Restricted Class members; it would also likely constitute speculative or short-term dealing prohibited under section 9(a) for all Representatives.
rules.evidence: Trading in Judo Securities for the purposes of this Policy includes dealing in, or procuring another person to deal in, Securities within the meaning of the Corporations Act.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named but would ordinarily be characterised as speculative or short-term dealing, which section 9(a) bans for all Representatives.
rules.evidence: Short term trading or speculative trading in Judo Securities, which means buying and selling Securities within a short time frame. Such trading may indicate that the relevant person's interests are not aligned with Judo's interests.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named individually but are captured as 'derivative products issued over or in respect of Judo Securities', an example of speculative or short-term dealing in section 9(a), and as Securities requiring clearance for Restricted Class members outside a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: entering into other speculative or short-term dealings (eg in derivative products issued over or in respect of Judo Securities).

rules.detail: Section 9(a) expressly lists derivative products issued over or in respect of Judo Securities as an example of prohibited speculative or short-term dealing, applicable to all Representatives.
rules.evidence: entering into other speculative or short-term dealings (eg in derivative products issued over or in respect of Judo Securities).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on margin lending arrangements in respect of Judo Securities for all Representatives, with no tier, vesting-state or clearance exception, and no exemption in the section 10 excluded-dealings list.
rules.evidence: Any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Judo Securities.

rules.detail: Granting security over Judo Securities to support any financing is banned as part of the 'other secured financing arrangements' prohibition; a charge or lien unconnected to financing is not named and is not captured elsewhere.
rules.evidence: Any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Judo Securities.

rules.detail: Blanket, unqualified ban on any secured financing arrangement in respect of Judo Securities for all Representatives. No exception in section 10 (which excludes only section 5 clearance and section 9(a) short-term dealing) extends to this ban, and no exemption authority exists.
rules.evidence: Any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Judo Securities.

rules.detail: Objective (not merely intention-based) 3-month test: buying and selling Securities on market within a 3-month period, or entering other speculative/short-term dealings (including derivatives), is prohibited for all Representatives. Carved out for securities acquired under an employee incentive scheme (including by vesting or exercise) traded within 3 months of that acquisition, and for excluded dealings under section 10.
rules.evidence: Short term or speculative trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period, and entering into other speculative or short-term dealings (eg in derivative products issued over or in respect of Judo Securities).

clearance.approver: CEO (Management Board member); Chair of the Board Audit Committee (Chair of the Board); Chair of the Board (CEO or other Board members); Company Secretary (all other Restricted Class members, or those requiring clearance under section 8)
clearance.evidence: If a clearance to deal is granted, clearance will last for 5 business days from the date given. ... A clearance to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board Audit Committee (Chair of the Board); Chair of the Board (other Board members)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of making any trade
clearance.evidence: Directors must provide the Company Secretary with written notifications of trading in Judo Securities (or any Securities of a related body corporate of Judo) within 2 business days of making any trade to allow any necessary disclosure(s) to be made to the ASX and/or ASIC.
Representatives who are not members of the Restricted Class do not require clearance to deal in Judo Securities outside a Blackout Period.

carve_outs: Securities acquired under an employee incentive scheme (including by way of vesting or exercise) traded within three months of acquisition
excluded dealing within the meaning of section 10
short_term.evidence: Short term or speculative trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period, and entering into other speculative or short-term dealings (eg in derivative products issued over or in respect of Judo Securities).

exceptions.approver: clearance under section 6 (CEO/Board Chair/Committee Chair/Company Secretary)
exceptions.evidence: where such a person is facing severe financial hardship and the sale of the Securities is the only practical method of overcoming the hardship

exceptions.approver: clearance under section 6 (CEO/Board Chair/Committee Chair/Company Secretary)
exceptions.evidence: where required by a court order, a court enforceable undertaking or an overriding legal or regulatory requirement to transfer, or accept a transfer of, the Securities.

transfers between a member of the Restricted Class and someone closely related to them e.g., a spouse, child, family company or family trust or to a super fund in respect of which written clearance from the Company Secretary has been provided
disposal of Securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back
disposal of rights under a pro-rata issue
acquisition of Securities under a pro-rata issue

acquisition of Securities under a security purchase plan or a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan where the Representative did not commence, withdraw or amend their participation during a Blackout Period
obtaining by a Board member of a share qualification

participation in, including acquisition of Securities or an interest in Securities under, an employee incentive scheme by way of acceptance of an invitation or grant under such an employee incentive scheme including an acquisition by a trustee or the vesting of any such Securities (but not the exercise of any such Security by a participant in the employee incentive scheme)

acquisition or disposal of Securities under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with this Policy where the Representative did not enter into the plan, cancel or amend the plan during a Blackout Period, and the plan does not permit the Representative to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan

indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a person in the Restricted Class dealing in Securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold, as part of its portfolio, Judo Securities.

exemption_authority: No exemption authority exists for the section 9(c) secured financing/margin lending ban or the section 9(b) hedging ban; the only relief mechanism in the policy is the exceptional-circumstances process in section 8 (severe financial hardship or court order), which applies to the Blackout Period dealing ban, not to these outright prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: As Judo is an authorised deposit-taking institution, Judo and its Securities are subject to the Financial Sector (Shareholdings) Act 1998 (Cth), meaning that any shareholding interest in Judo which exceeds 20% could attract penalties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank's hedge position or enforcement rights under the collar could result in it holding a stake exceeding 20% of Judo, FSSA approval would be required before entering or enforcing the structure.

bespoke_clauses.topic: excluded dealings do not reach section 9
bespoke_clauses.clause: The following types of dealings are excluded from the operation of section 5 of this policy, do not require approval under section 6 and do not breach the prohibition on short term trading in section 0
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: None of the section 10 excluded dealings (e.g. plan vesting, pro-rata issues) lift the absolute section 9(b)/(c) bans on hedging or secured financing, so there is no carve-out route around the collar prohibition even for vested plan shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: associate definition limited to blackout periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: a company or trust controlled by any of them; and a spouse ... a close relative or a person financially dependent on, or acting in concert, with any of them [applies] for the purpose of any Blackout Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The extension of the policy to controlled entities, spouses and associates is expressed to apply only for Blackout Period purposes; outside a Blackout Period a family trust or controlled entity holding the collared shares may sit outside the policy's clearance and hedging provisions, though the secured-financing ban's 'in respect of Judo Securities' wording is not itself tier-limited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If clearance to deal is refused, the person seeking clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A refusal affecting a proposed collar cannot be disclosed to the bank, which complicates timing and structuring discussions around clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a clearance to deal is granted, clearance will last for 5 business days from the date given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared derivative leg (were the secured financing ban not fatal) would need to be priced and executed within 5 business days of clearance.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable under this policy. Section 9(c) imposes a blanket, unconditional ban on 'any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Judo Securities' for all Representatives (including Directors and other Restricted Class members), with no clearance route, tier or vesting-state exception, and none of the section 10 excluded dealings reach this prohibition, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares cannot be put in place. Section 9(b) separately bans all hedging transactions that limit the economic risk of holding Judo Securities, again without exception, so the put/call legs would themselves be prohibited outright rather than merely gated by clearance. Even setting the bans aside, the derivative legs would otherwise be dealing in Securities (which expressly include derivatives), requiring prior written clearance from the CEO, Board Chair, Audit Committee Chair or Company Secretary for Restricted Class members, valid for only 5 business days, and barred altogether during the FY-end, half-year and AGM Blackout Periods except for severe financial hardship or court order. There is no exemption authority for the section 9 prohibitions, so no lawful structuring path exists for a bank-funded collar while this policy stands.
